title: No new revelation — only a fallible hand-to-hand chain Augustine calls interminable
source_text: XLIII. Sed quantacunque authoritas seu Concilio, seu Papae tribuatur, agnoscunt doctissimi & probatissimi quique inter Pontificios, Ecclesiam hodie non regi novis revelationibus, nec Papam, neque Concilium immediate a Deo discere quid Apostoli tradiderint. Unde ergo istud certo discere possunt? Profecto nihil ipsis hic dicendum superest, nisi, quod & revera dicunt, nempe, Papam, sive Concilium id habere ex voce & testimonio Doctorum Ecclesiae, qui de manu in manum hoc vel illud acceperunt a priscis illis Doctoribus qui Apostolorum fuerunt auditores. Sed jam pluribus instantiis, & ex ipsa adversariorum confessione manifestum fecimus antiquissimos Ecclesiae Doctores in traditionibus recipiendis atque commendandis saepe fuisse deceptos, atque hallucinatos, & eorum plurimos communi consensu tanquam dogma & institutum Apostolicum admisisse, quod Ecclesia Romana hodie rejicit & damnat. Quomodo ergo certam fidem eorum testimonia facere potuerunt Conciliis & Pontificibus saeculorum posteriorum? Et quomodo traditiones a Patribus acceptae respectu Pontificum & Conciliorum ipsorum possunt haberi pro certa regula ex qua controversias propositas dijudicent, non minus quam ex ipsa Scriptura? Et jam hoc ipsum quaeritur, qua ratione tolli possit incertitudo quae nascitur ex Patrum & priscorum illorum Ecclesiae Doctorum variis testimoniis & pugnantibus inter se sententiis, quum agitur de iis quae Apostoli tradiderunt. Quare ea merito dicit Augustinus loco citato: Quod quum ad Apostolorum traditionem recurritur & circa ipsam pugnatur, Interminabilis est ista contentio, generans lites, non finiens quaestiones.
pass_a_gloss: But whatever authority is attributed to Council or to Pope, the most learned and approved among the Pontiffs acknowledge that the Church today is not ruled by new revelations, nor do Pope or Council learn immediately from God what the Apostles handed down. From where then can they learn that with certainty? Truly nothing remains for them to say here except what they actually do say: namely, that Pope or Council has it from the voice and testimony of the Church's Doctors, who received this or that from hand to hand from those early Doctors who were hearers of the Apostles. But already by many instances, and from the adversaries' own confession, we have made plain that the most ancient doctors of the Church in receiving and recommending traditions were often deceived and hallucinating, and that many of them by common consent admitted as Apostolic dogma and institute what the Roman Church today rejects and condemns. How then could their testimonies make certain faith for the Councils and Pontiffs of later ages? And how can traditions received from the Fathers, with respect to the Pontiffs and Councils themselves, be held as a certain rule by which to judge proposed controversies, no less than from Scripture itself? And now this very thing is asked: by what reason can the uncertainty be removed which arises from the various testimonies and mutually conflicting opinions of the Fathers and those early doctors of the Church, when it is a question of what the Apostles handed down. Wherefore Augustine rightly says in the place cited: When recourse is had to the Apostles' tradition and fighting goes on about it itself, That contention is interminable, breeding quarrels, not ending questions.
pass_b_english: Even Rome's best grant: the Church is not run by new revelations, and neither Pope nor Council learns immediately from God what the Apostles taught.
Their only remaining answer: hand-to-hand testimony of doctors back to hearers of the Apostles.
But we have already shown — and Rome's own history admits — that the earliest doctors often erred in receiving 'apostolic' traditions, and by common consent held as apostolic what Rome now condemns.
How then can that chain give later Councils and popes certain faith, or serve as a rule equal to Scripture for settling controversies?

The uncertainty of conflicting Father-witness is exactly what still needs removing. Augustine, in the place already cited: when the fight turns on apostolic tradition itself, the contention is interminable — it breeds quarrels and does not end questions.

choices.english: in the place already cited (Aug. to Casulanus)
